howto.name: Add the PDF
howto.text: Drop or select a PDF of up to 500 pages and 500 MB, such as a résumé or paper you are screening, or a redacted document before you share it. It is uploaded over HTTPS and checked on the PrivaTools server in isolated temporary per-request storage. The page preview is drawn on your device.

howto.name: Run the check
howto.text: Click Check for hidden text. Every page is examined for text a reader cannot see but a program still reads: text set to be invisible or fully transparent, text in the colour of what lies behind it, text too small to read, text off the page or cut away by a clipping path, text in layers that are switched off, text under a box, shape or image drawn over it, text in hidden comments and form fields, and redaction marks that were never applied.

howto.name: Read the findings
howto.text: Each finding gives the page, the reason and the exact words, and is highlighted on the page preview; the counts show how many of each kind were found. Invisible text over a scanned page image, which OCR software adds so a scan can be searched, is listed separately and is not counted as hidden text.

howto.name: Fix it, or keep the report
howto.text: Download the report as text or JSON. To remove what was found, use Redact PDF, which deletes the text under the boxes you draw, or Sanitize Document, which removes hidden layers along with scripts and attachments. A clean result means none of these checks matched, not that the file is safe in every way.

faq.q: How do I find hidden text in a PDF?
faq.a: Run the file through this checker. It reads every character the way text extraction does, then tests whether a reader can actually see it: how it is drawn (text render mode 3 or 7 draws nothing), its opacity, its colour against what is drawn behind it, its size, whether it lies on the visible page or inside a clipping path, whether its layer is switched on, and whether a box, shape or image was drawn over it. Where the answer depends on how the page looks, the page is rendered and the words count as hidden only if their area shows no ink at all, so readable text is not reported.

faq.q: Can it find hidden AI prompts in a résumé or a paper?
faq.a: Yes, when they are hidden in any of the ways it checks. Instructions such as "ignore all previous instructions" have been hidden in résumés and papers as white or tiny text, where screening software and AI models read them but people do not. The checker shows each hidden passage and its exact words. It cannot tell whether hidden text is malicious, only that it is there, so read it and decide; white text can also be leftover formatting.

faq.q: How do I check whether a redacted PDF is really redacted?
faq.a: Check the redacted file before you share it. A black box drawn over text hides it from the eye but leaves the words in the file, where copying, search and AI tools still find them; the checker reports those words as text under a shape or image. Areas marked for redaction but never applied are reported too, as is text under a picture of the page laid on top. A real redaction removes the text, so nothing is found under the box. Redact PDF removes the text under the boxes you draw.

faq.q: Why is invisible text over my scanned pages listed separately?
faq.a: OCR software makes a scan searchable by laying invisible text over the page image, so that text is expected. It is listed as an OCR text layer, with a sample of its words, and is not counted as hidden text. Invisible words that sit over a blank part of the page image, where the picture shows nothing, are reported as hidden text.

faq.q: Does a clean result mean the PDF is safe?
faq.a: No. It means none of these checks matched. The checker does not look inside attachments, scripts or metadata, cannot see text drawn with a font whose letters show as different letters, and does not notice text hidden by a soft mask or by a transparency group's own opacity, or under a shape that covers each letter only in part. Sanitize Document removes scripts, attachments and hidden layers, and Strip Metadata removes document properties.

Yes. The check runs on the PrivaTools server, because it needs the drawing order, colour and opacity of every character, which the PDF engine in your browser does not report. The file is uploaded over HTTPS, checked in isolated temporary per-request storage by a separate process with memory and time limits, and deleted when the check ends; a background sweep clears anything an interrupted request leaves behind. The report is sent back to you and not stored. Your file is not changed.

Up to 500 pages and 500 MB per file, and 90 seconds of checking; split a longer document with Split PDF and check the parts. Password-protected PDFs must be unlocked first, and the site's fair-use rate limits apply.
